title: Rishabh Pant Ruled Out of Final India A Match, Doubtful for Wellington Test
excerpt: Pant will miss the November 7 India A match in Lincoln with a left-side strain, and his place in the first Test against New Zealand on November 19 depends on a fitness evaluation that has no confirmed timeline.
body:
• Rishabh Pant will miss the third and final unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A in Lincoln, starting November 7, as he continues to recover from a left-side strain.
  • Pant is also doubtful for the first Test against New Zealand, starting November 19 at the Basin Reserve in Wellington; he was named in India's 16-member Test squad subject to fitness clearance.
  • Pant has resumed skill training at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru and is pain-free, but there is no confirmed timeline for his return to competitive cricket.
  • Dhruv Jurel, who made an unbeaten 99 for India A in the second match at Christchurch, is the keeper in form if Pant is not cleared in time.

Rishabh Pant has been ruled out of the third and final unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A, and his availability for the first Test against New Zealand is now in serious doubt. The four-day India A match begins on November 7 in Lincoln, and Pant will play no part in it, according to reports — he has now missed all three matches of a series that was meant to give him red-ball preparation before the senior tour.

Pant picked up a left-side strain in early October while captaining Rest of India against Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup in Srinagar. He missed the first two India A matches in New Zealand because of the same injury, with Kumar Kushagra named as his replacement for those games, and Sportskeeda reported that his absence from the Lincoln match is a precautionary measure while the BCCI medical team waits for full clearance.

Training again, but no return date

The update is not all negative. According to a PTI report carried by Khel Now, Pant has resumed skill training at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru and is currently not experiencing any pain.

https://x.com/Anurag9793/status/2116921873879765011

"Although Pant has resumed skill training and is experiencing no pain, there is still no confirmed timeline for his return to competitive cricket."

— BCCI source, quoted by PTI

CricTracker reported that Pant must complete three skill training sessions alongside four match simulation sessions before a formal fitness evaluation can be conducted. Only after those sessions will the medical team assess his batting and wicketkeeping and decide on a return-to-play plan. Reports around October 26 had suggested he was on course to return for the third India A match, but updated assessments by November 1 reversed that expectation.

What it means for Wellington

Pant was named in India's 16-member Test squad for the New Zealand series, but his selection was made subject to a fitness clearance from the BCCI medical team, and his place in the playing eleven for Wellington depends on that clearance arriving before the match. The first Test begins on November 19 at the Basin Reserve, with the second match of the two-Test series following from November 27.

If Pant is not cleared, Dhruv Jurel is the obvious stand-in. Jurel has been the standout wicketkeeper-batter for India A in Pant's absence, striking an unbeaten 99 in the second unofficial Test at Christchurch — form that strengthens his case for a Test start. As of November 1, there has been no official announcement of a squad change or a confirmed replacement, and the decision is expected to wait until Pant completes his prescribed assessment sessions.

For India, the stakes are clear: Pant is one of their most important overseas Test batters, and going into a two-Test series in New Zealand without him would reshape both the middle order and the wicketkeeping plans. The next update will come from the medical team's evaluation, not from the selection room.
